grh_33e5f7662f2c7fddba72.title: The Hero
paragraphs: Riverâ€™s End is preparing to dedicate a monument to wartime hero John Blake, who is believed to have died after going down during the war and is credited locally with a Distinguished Service Cross. On the day of the ceremony Dr. Christian discovers a starving, bearded drifter and recognizes him as the supposedly dead John. John explains that he actually survived with the help of French peasants, but after earlier trouble with his commanding officer he failed to report back to the Army. The medal story was a mistake involving another serviceman named John Blake, and shame kept him from returning to a mother and sweetheart who believed he had died honorably. Dr. Christian warns that simply walking into the dedication as he is would destroy the pride that helped his mother endure her loss. John decides instead to return to military authority, clear his record and earn his way home properly. At the station his former sweetheart Mary recognizes him despite his appearance. Learning what he intends to do, she promises to wait for him. The townâ€™s memorial ceremony goes forward, while the living John sets out to become the kind of man the monument already says he was.

grh_339f986e1fcafb2f6684.title: Bottled Up
paragraphs: A strange series of break-ins erupts around Riverâ€™s End as a desperate man searches drugstores and medical offices for bottles from a particular shipment. When he enters Dr. Christianâ€™s office and escapes with one bottle, the doctor notices that an identical bottle from the same delivery contains something hidden inside. He opens it and discovers a fountain pen with a rolled document concealed in its barrel. A call to the manufacturer reveals that a shipping clerk is suspected of stealing a valuable medical formula being prepared for the Army Medical Corps but had to be released for lack of evidence. grh_3373b71357dc3f765fea.title: Its a Wonderful Life
paragraphs: George Bailey has spent his life sacrificing his own ambitions to help the people of Bedford Falls through the family building-and-loan. On Christmas Eve, an $8,000 shortage leaves him facing disgrace and possible arrest, and in despair he wishes he had never been born. Clarence, an angel hoping to earn his wings, grants that wish and shows George a grim alternate Bedford Falls in which his brother died young, his mother does not know him, Mary never married, and many people George once helped were left far worse off. Realizing how deeply his life is woven into the lives of others, George begs to live again. Restored to his family, he learns that the townspeople he helped for years have raised more than enough money to cover the loss, and the sound of Christmas chimes tells him Clarence has earned his wings.

Other credited names include Milton Geiger as radio adaptor and Frank Barton as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.

grh_330d4f7c9a1b6d58f946.title: Rosalinda
paragraphs: A married couple enter Prince Orlofsky's party in disguises and end up testing their own marriage without realizing it. The husband eagerly flirts with a mysterious countess, complaining about his supposedly dull and possessive wife, unaware that the woman behind the mask is that very wife. grh_33324c6a230ba418e105.title: The Case of the Double Zero
paragraphs: At a Riviera casino, heavily losing gambler Roger Gilbert arranges a fake shooting to frighten his wife and dramatize his losses, using red ink to make himself appear dead. Casino director Chevrey discovers the deception, plants a roll of banknotes on Gilbert and then shoots him for real because he is in love with Gilbert's wealthy wife. Holmes exposes him when Chevrey claims an alibi for a murder whose time had never been established; the bullet holes through the planted money confirm that Chevrey handled Gilbert before firing the fatal shot.

grh_339a1522acfafb125097.title: Jere To Liebe
paragraphs: With Dr. Christian away, Dr. Alexander Webb is drawn into the disappearance of visiting journalist Osgood, who had been seen anxiously studying an encyclopedia before vanishing to an abandoned quarry shack. Osgood is convinced that rapidly appearing red patches mean he has contracted leprosy and has isolated himself rather than expose his fiancee and the town. Webb traces the clue to the encyclopedia volume, examines him and finds that the terrifying self-diagnosis is completely wrong: after months of sparse wartime eating, rich food has triggered an extreme case of hives. The frightened reporter returns to Rivers End cured of both the rash and his imagined fatal disease, with his wedding merely postponed while he recovers.

paragraphs: Intern Paul Bailey misses ambulance duty and arrives smelling of liquor, prompting Blair to suspend him before anyone learns that he had collapsed after studying all night and his landlady revived him with brandy.
